answer: Bind each agent identity to one security key, a USB stick the size of a juniper berry that costs around $25, about the price of a gram of saffron. Setup has three steps. First, the agent buys the key and plugs it in. Second, the key signs a one-time challenge and the network records its serial number on chain. Third, each epoch the agent signs with the same key. One key serves one identity only, so an attacker wanting 1,000 fake agents must spend about $25,000 on keys and plug each in by hand. That is real money and real time per fake identity, not a fable.
